verifier_note: Checked 29 entries against primary sources retrieved 2026-09-25: EMNLP/CVPR/NeurIPS/ICML/ECCV/SIGGRAPH-Asia/ICCV paper pages and official proceedings, GitHub license-API and raw-LICENSE fetches, PyPI, and Hugging Face model cards, plus the ASME/GD&T standard pages and the Thomas & Johnston animation-principles source for the eval-qa design-analogy entries. 19 confirmed, 7 corrected, 3 unfindable, 0 refuted. Every author list, paper title, venue, core mechanism, and headline license (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/CC-BY-NC-SA/Stability/Tencent community terms) that was checked matched its primary source, including the one entry (SD-piXL) flagged going in as the likeliest fabrication, which turned out genuine. The lane's systemic weakness is a recurring pattern of appending one unsourced, specific-sounding secondary detail onto an otherwise rock-solid primary claim: DISTS's venue year (2020 arXiv/early-access date presented as the citable venue, actually IEEE TPAMI 2022), MEt3R's dependency license (DUSt3R is CC-BY-NC-SA, the ShareAlike clause was dropped), MLLM-as-a-Judge's 'permissive' license claim (the repo ships no LICENSE file at all), Hunyuan3D-2.1's invented attribution phrase ('Created with Hunyuan 3D-2.1' appears nowhere in the license), and TRELLIS.2's Windows/WSL2 guidance (the repo never mentions Windows anywhere). A second, distinct weakness sits in the four 'STUDY-038/STUDY-007' entries: internal-only self-referential status wrappers ('Analogist Verifier hold-with-limit', 'Flip 486: 0') that carry no externally checkable content of their own, plus a 'silhouette' conflation caught independently in two separate entries — only staging and solid drawing are actually among Thomas & Johnston's twelve named principles; silhouette readability is a corollary of staging, not a distinct principle. No harmful or destructive advice was found in the lane; the three unfindable entries are all self-declared on-rig measurements against a Linux-only official model, which is exactly the case the brief's on-rig carve-out anticipates.

verdicts.verify_note: ASME Y14.3 ('Orthographic and Pictorial Views', asme.org) is real, governs multiview registration/scale. 'STUDY-038'/'Flip 486' wrapper is internal status data, not externally checkable.
ASME Y14.3 (asme.org) codifies the multiview system of orthographic drawing — fixed views sharing scale/registration/alignment — matching the front/side/top analogy exactly.
Hessel et al., EMNLP 2021 (ACL Anthology) confirmed: rescaled cosine similarity, beats CIDEr/SPICE on human correlation. jmhessel/clipscore=MIT, openai/CLIP license API=MIT.
ASME Y14.5 GD&T datum reference frame (3 mutually perpendicular datum planes, primary/secondary/tertiary hierarchy) matches the shared-anchor/one-contact-point analogy.
Ding/Ma/Wang/Simoncelli, VGG conv1_2-conv5_3, MIT license, DISTS-pytorch on PyPI all confirmed (arxiv.org/abs/2004.07728). Venue year is wrong — see corrections.

corrections.claim: Venue is IEEE TPAMI 2022 (Vol. 44, No. 5, pp. 2567-2581), not 2020 — 2020 is only the arXiv preprint / IEEE early-access DOI date, not the citable journal publication.
